markdown_report:
The best next step is a position-preserving recency probe for the existing NextItNet adapter. At 10% research progress, establishing trustworthy intervention measurements is more feasible than adding architectural complexity without evidence.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Electronics has a 12.27% sampled negative-over-positive rate, versus 0.96% for CDs_and_Vinyl. This motivates category-specific investigation, but does not establish validation performance. (2) Deletion and compaction change surviving items’ positions. Observed effects can therefore mix item removal with altered convolutional context. (3) Qualitative feedback suggests insufficient attention to current purpose. Histories support testing recency sensitivity, while ownership, compatibility and unmet needs remain unobserved.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [NextItNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163) expands structural history coverage through dilated causal convolutions. Structural reach alone does not demonstrate effective use of distant interactions. (2) [Activation-patching research](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/06a52a54c8ee03cd86771136bc91eb1f-Abstract-Conference.html) shows that corruption choices affect localization. Intervention controls are consequently essential before attributing a ranking change to recency. (3) [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show that sampled metrics can misrepresent ranking comparisons. Exact catalog ranks complement, but cannot replace, the pinned benchmark.

**Framework and directions.** Organize evidence along three directions: intervention validity, internal mechanism localization, and recommendation relevance. Within each, distinguish observable training sensitivity, qualitative hypotheses and held-out performance. The present gap is controlled sensitivity evidence; neither sampled margins nor user narratives identify a repair.

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means more implementation effort.

- **Matched lag replacements — 5/8/4.** Originality: useful task-specific control; established perturbation method. Potential: supports focused repairs; synthetic replacements may be unnatural. Difficulty: existing interfaces suffice; matching needs coverage checks.
- **Residual-block activation recovery — 6/7/7.** Originality: adapts causal tracing; method already exists. Potential: localizes useful computation; recovery need not imply necessity. Difficulty: hooks enable implementation; alignment and normalization are delicate.
- **Evidence-backed relevance audit — 4/6/5.** Originality: connects complaints to observable content; rubric design is familiar. Potential: distinguishes topicality from specificity; sparse descriptions limit coverage. Difficulty: simple labels; credible assessment requires independent annotation.

**Selected algorithm.** Sample fixed training prefixes and compare clean histories with frequency-matched replacements in recent and older lag bands. Preserve length, padding, occupied positions and the terminal item; match the number of changed positions. Freeze eligible candidates using the original prefix, retaining the target, and compute exact chunked ranks under a documented tie rule. Report paired rank changes, top-ten overlap, matching coverage and user-bootstrap intervals. These measure intervention sensitivity, not generalization.

Preserve `DiagnosisProbe`, `run_full_diagnosis`, the interpreter callable and ModelView interfaces. Use the maximum nonpadding index, restore model modes and random states, and retain one NextItNet checkpoint per category. Any subsequent repair must earn selection through unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10.

idea.description: Add position-preserving, frequency-matched lag replacement probes to the existing NextItNet diagnostic adapter. Compare paired changes in exact eligible-catalog target rank across recent and older history bands while keeping candidate eligibility fixed.
idea.motivation: Existing deletion probes can confound removed information with positional changes. The supplied feedback motivates a recency hypothesis, but the current training margins and qualitative observations do not establish its mechanism or predict a successful repair.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Use the actual view.model through log2feats and predict_score; do not train an auxiliary predictor. Build item-frequency bins exclusively from training histories. Exclude padding, the target and original-prefix items from replacement pools; report unmatched cases instead of silently relaxing controls. Exclude the terminal item from the primary comparison and label this scope explicitly. Match recent/older intervention counts and frequency-bin distributions where feasible. Freeze candidate eligibility from each original prefix, excluding previously observed items except the target. Count greater scores in catalog chunks and resolve exact ties using a fixed documented item-ID ordering. Read features at the maximum nonpadding index, never count-1. Include identity replacements and causality checks; apply outside-receptive-field controls only when structurally applicable. Bootstrap users with their prefixes kept together, and return null intervals when coverage is inadequate. Restore module modes and Python, NumPy, CPU and CUDA RNG states. Return measured metrics, definitions, denominators and unavailable-data reasons; do not infer ownership or compatibility. Preserve seeds, routing, DATA_DIR, training limits, checkpoint/predictor consistency and the pinned evaluator. This proposal changes diagnostics only and requires no predictor architecture change.

originality.positive: Combines fixed eligibility, lag matching and position preservation into a concrete family-aware diagnostic experiment.
originality.negative: Controlled perturbations and paired ranking measurements are established techniques; novelty is primarily their careful integration.

future_potential.positive: Provides a reusable basis for deciding which NextItNet context-use hypotheses deserve limited training budget.
future_potential.negative: Sensitivity to synthetic replacements may not reflect natural behavior or identify changes that improve validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses existing scoring interfaces and leaves the trained model and embedded predictor unchanged.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable matching, fixed candidate masks, exact ties and restoration of diagnostic state require careful implementation.

related_work.title: NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Uses residual dilated causal convolutions for sequential recommendation.
Provides the backbone whose context sensitivity the proposed probes measure.
limitations: Structural receptive-field coverage does not establish which interactions determine a particular prediction.

related_work.title: ICLR 2024 activation-patching research supplied in the search results
contributions: Supports controlling corruption methods and measurement choices when interpreting intervention results.
limitations: Does not establish the validity of these proposed NextItNet interventions.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation can distort comparisons between recommendation models.
limitations: Does not justify replacing this task's pinned sampled validation metric with catalog-wide diagnostics.

related_work.title: Uncertainty in Online Experiments with Dependent Data
contributions: Motivates accounting for dependence when estimating uncertainty.
Supports retaining a user's paired observations together during resampling.
limitations: User bootstrap intervals do not capture training-seed variability, all item dependence or adaptive validation-selection bias.
